title: Your AI Isn’t the Problem. Your Infrastructure Is. — Jiachen Jiang, Coder
talk_summary: A Coder PM walks through three real agent incidents (Replit deleting a production DB, a Copilot session-token compromise exfiltrating banking data, and the Nx supply-chain prompt injection) and argues the fix is infrastructure controls, not smarter models. He ranks six layered controls: isolated remote workspaces, short-lived scoped credentials, identity-aligned access control, a model proxy layer, agent sandboxing, and audit logging outside the agent's reach.

takeaways.technique: Isolated remote workspaces as the top-leverage control
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents execute in ephemeral, code-defined remote workspaces with no route to production or personal credentials, so blast radius is one disposable container instead of a laptop or prod.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If the agent had been executing in an isolated remote workspace without a route to production, it doesn't matter what the prompt said

takeaways.what_they_do: Replace long-lived broad tokens with credentials that auto-expire and are issued per task, so a leaked or misused token can't do more than the task.
takeaways.evidence_quote: having a credential that can expire on its own or only carries the scope of the task itself makes it impossible to make a delete

takeaways.technique: Model proxy layer that inspects/filters/logs calls
takeaways.what_they_do: A proxy between model and agent inspects, filters, and logs every call, stripping injected instructions from external content and flagging suspicious requests before they're answered.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the model proxy layer which sits between the model and the agent to inspect, filter, and log every call that's going between them

takeaways.technique: Audit logging the agent cannot alter
takeaways.what_they_do: Every agentic action is attributable to a human and logged outside the agent's reach, with real-time alerting rather than post-hoc log diving.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We need to have every agentic action attributable to a human being should be logged somewhere outside of the agent's own reach

takeaways.technique: Agent sandboxing as a filesystem/network firewall
takeaways.what_they_do: Restrict agent filesystem and network access so a compromised or misbehaving agent has limited blast radius even if an instruction lands.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Agent sandboxing can be thought of as a firewall for agents restrictions on the file system and the network

takeaways.technique: Identity-aligned access control for AI tooling
takeaways.what_they_do: AI tools inherit the same identity-provider enforcement as humans instead of having a parallel subscription with its own door and broader access.
takeaways.evidence_quote: AI tooling should inherit the same identity provider enforcement as human access. Shouldn't be some parallel subscription with a door of its own
